latest.title: Amazon ECS Managed Instances Now Supports AWS Trainium and Inferentia
latest.description: Amazon ECS Managed Instances now supports Inferentia2, Trainium1, and Trainium2 via the capacity provider, with automatic Neuron device assignment through a single resourceRequirements entry in the task definition. This post walks through the setup — including a discrepancy between the announcement and the Developer Guide — along with use cases, a comparison with EKS and SageMaker, and cost considerations.

latest.title: The Semantic Foundation — Why Your Data Agent Needs More Than RAG
latest.description: The promise of "ask your data anything" has been around for years. The reality? Most implementations hallucinate metrics, confuse business terms, and break the moment questions get domain-specific. Explore why the semantic layer — not the model — is the missing piece, and see how AutoScout24 built a production-grade data agent (Omnio) that answers "why" questions across 13 data domains using governed context, ontologies, and evaluation-gated releases

latest.title: I Talked to 16 AWS Builders and They All Said the Same Three Things
latest.description: After months of conversations with architects, scientists, and engineers building AI systems at AWS, three patterns kept surfacing: the craft migrated from writing code to designing trust, one person now orchestrates what used to take a team, and nobody has converged on how to verify agentic output at scale.

latest.title: Sem experiência? Seus projetos pessoais são o seu currículo
latest.description: Todo estudante de tecnologia já esbarrou nisso: você se inscreve na vaga, participa das etapas do processo mas no final recebe mais um feedback dizendo que preferiram seguir com outro candidato. A saída é mais acessível do que parece — projetos pessoais bem construídos comunicam habilidade real antes mesmo de você entrar no mercado. Aqui você encontra um caminho direto para montar um portfólio técnico relevante, com sugestões práticas para desenvolvimento, cloud, segurança, dados, DevOps e IA.

latest.title: AWS Networking from Scratch: VPC, Subnets, CIDR, IP Types, and Linux on EC2
latest.description:
I remember the first time I opened the AWS VPC console. There were subnets, route tables, internet gateways, NAT gateways, CIDRs, elastic IPs — and I had no idea how any of it connected. It looked like someone had taken a real data center and just... digitized the chaos.

So let me walk you through all of it the way I wish someone had walked me through it: in plain language, with real reasoning, not a wall of definitions.

latest.title: From Operational to Analytical, Part 2b: Letting It Run
latest.description: A scheduled, unattended prune of the hot side of a CDC pipeline — gated on the cold archive having actually received the rows about to be deleted. Walks through the safety-check pattern, three design choices that distinguish a working version from a naive one, and a one-week soak.

latest.title: Processamento em Lote Sem Servidor (Serverless Batch Processing): MapReduce em Hiperescala com AWS Step Functions Distributed Map
latest.description: O artigo orienta a construção de pipelines de dados em hiperescala utilizando o AWS Step Functions Distributed Map para orquestrar paralelismo extremo sobre arquivos massivos no Amazon S3. Direcionado a engenheiros de software, o material explora a contenção de falhas em nível de item, a mitigação do estrangulamento de APIs downstream através de concorrência controlada e a aplicação da Arquitetura Hexagonal em nós de trabalho (workers), garantindo resiliência absoluta.

latest.title: The Code Is Still Yours: Application-Layer Security for AWS Lambda
latest.description: Part 4 of the Lambda Security Series moves past configuration to the code itself. It covers why every event source is untrusted input (injection, XXE, SSRF, path traversal), how execution-role credentials are stolen straight from the runtime environment, insecure deserialization, dependency and supply-chain risk, Amazon Inspector code and image scanning, runtime secrets handling, logging without leaking, and the GuardDuty/CloudTrail/X-Ray detection you need when prevention fails.

ASET (Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth) is a scientific claim verification engine built  for the AI era — where information can be generated instantly, but trust cannot, to address the growing problem of hallucinated citations and  AI-generated information.
